questions.q: When did Nebuchadnezzar have dreams that troubled his mind so that he could not sleep?
questions.a: This occurred in the second year of his reign.

questions.q: Why did the king summon the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans?
questions.a: The king wanted these men to tell him about his dreams.

questions.q: What did the king tell his advisors about his dream?
questions.a: The king told them that he had dreamed a dream and that he wanted to know what it meant.

questions.q: What did the Chaldeans ask the king to do?
questions.a: The Chaldeans asked the king to tell them the dream so they could tell him what it meant.

questions.q: What did the king specifically want the wise men to do?
questions.a: The king wanted the wise men to reveal the dream to him and also to interpret the meaning of the dream for the king.

questions.q: What did the king say would happen to the wise men if they failed to tell the king his dream and interpret it for him?
questions.a: The king said that if they failed, their bodies would be cut into pieces and their houses would be turned into piles of rubbish.

questions.q: What did the king say he would do for the person or people who revealed the dream to him and interpreted it?
questions.a: The king said he would give that person or persons gifts, a reward, and great honor.

questions.q: What did the advisors say again to the king?
questions.a: They said again that the king should tell them the dream, and they would tell him what it meant.

questions.q: What did the king say the advisors were doing?
questions.a: The king said that the advisors were trying to get more time because they knew he would carry out what he had said.

questions.q: What did the king say the advisors had agreed to do?
questions.a: The king said they had agreed to tell him a false explanation until the situation changed.

questions.q: Who did the Chaldeans say could do what the king asked concerning his dream?
questions.a: The Chaldeans said that there was not a man on earth who could meet the king’s demand, only the gods could do that.

questions.q: How did the king feel after the advisors said they could not tell him his dream?
questions.a: The king became extremely angry, and he commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be executed.

questions.q: After the wise men’s reply to Nebuchadnezzar, what did the king decree?
questions.a: The king decreed that all those known for their wisdom were to be put to death.

questions.q: How did Daniel interact with Arioch when he came to Daniel?
questions.a: Daniel replied with prudence and discretion to Arioch. He asked Arioch why the king’s decree was so urgent.

questions.q: Who was Arioch?
questions.a: He was the captain of the king’s guard, the one who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.

questions.q: What did Daniel request after speaking with Arioch?
questions.a: Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time so that he could tell the king what his dream meant.

questions.q: What did Daniel do when he went to his house?
questions.a: Daniel told his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what had happened.

questions.q: What did Daniel ask his friends to seek from the God of heaven?
questions.a: Daniel asked them to seek mercy from the God of heaven about the mystery, so that he and his friends would not be killed with the other wise men of Babylon.

questions.q: What did Daniel do after the secret was revealed to him?
questions.a: Daniel praised the God of heaven.

questions.q: What did Daniel say about God’s wisdom and power?
questions.a: Daniel said that wisdom and power belong to God, and that God’s name should be blessed forever.

questions.q: What did Daniel say God does with kings and with wisdom?
questions.a: Daniel said that God removes kings and sets up kings, and that God gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who understand.

questions.q: What did Daniel say God reveals and knows?
questions.a: Daniel said God reveals deep and hidden things, and that God knows what is in the darkness because the light is with him.

questions.q: For what did Daniel thank the God of his ancestors?
questions.a: Daniel thanked the God of his ancestors for the wisdom and power the God of his ancestors had given him.

questions.q: Who did Daniel go see after the secret was revealed to him?
questions.a: Daniel went in to see Arioch.

questions.q: What did Daniel tell Arioch?
questions.a: Daniel told Arioch not to kill the wise men in Babylon. Daniel told Arioch to escort him before the king so Daniel could tell the king the dream’s meaning.

questions.q: What did Arioch tell the king about Daniel?
questions.a: Arioch told the king that he had found a man from the captives of Judah who could tell the king the interpretation of his dream.

questions.q: What did the king ask Daniel?
questions.a: The king asked Daniel whether he was able to tell him the dream that he had seen and its interpretation.

questions.q: What did Daniel say about the wise men, enchanters, magicians, and diviners?
questions.a: Daniel said that they were not able to show the king the mystery that he had asked about.

questions.q: When Daniel was brought in to the king, who did Daniel say could reveal the mystery the king had demanded?
questions.a: Daniel said there is a God who lives in the heavens, who reveals secrets.

questions.q: In general what did Daniel say the king’s dream was about?
questions.a: Daniel said the dream was about what would happen in the days to come.

questions.q: What did Daniel say the king had been thinking about while on his bed?
questions.a: Daniel said the king had been thinking about what will happen in the future, and that God had revealed to him what that will be.

questions.q: Why was the dream revealed to Daniel?
questions.a: The dream was revealed to Daniel so that the king might understand the meaning and know the thoughts deep within himself.

questions.q: What did the statue that the king saw in his dream look like?
questions.a: The statue was large and had a head of gold, a chet and arms of silver, its middle and thighs were bronze, its legs of iron and its feet part iron and part clay.

questions.q: What were the feet of the statue made of?
questions.a: The feet of the statue were made partly of iron and partly of clay.

questions.q: What happened to the statue the king saw in his dream?
questions.a: The king saw a stone cut, but not by human hands. The stone struck the statue’s feet and the whole statue shattered into pieces which the wind carried away.

questions.q: What happened to the stone that struck the statue?
questions.a: The stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

questions.q: What did Daniel say he and his friends would do after telling the king his dream?
questions.a: Daniel said they would tell the king the interpretation of the dream.

questions.q: What did Daniel say God had given to the king?
questions.a: Daniel said God had given the king the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.

questions.q: Who was the head of gold?
questions.a: King Nebuchadnezzar was the head of gold.

questions.q: What did Daniel say would happen after the king’s kingdom?
questions.a: Daniel said another kingdom would arise after his, and then a third kingdom of bronze would rule over all the earth.

questions.q: What did Daniel say the fourth kingdom would be like?
questions.a: Daniel said the fourth kingdom would be strong like iron, and it would crush and break all the other kingdoms.

questions.q: What did the feet and toes made of clay and iron mean?
questions.a: They meant that the kingdom would be divided, partly strong like iron and partly weak, because the king saw iron mixed with clay.

questions.q: What did the iron and clay in the toes of the statue represent?
questions.a: They represented that part of the kingdom would be strong and part of it would be brittle.

questions.q: What did Daniel say would happen even though the kingdoms would mix themselves by marriage?
questions.a: Daniel said the kingdoms would not stay united with each other, just as iron does not mix with clay.

questions.q: What will the God of heaven do in the days of the kingdom that is partly iron and partly clay?
questions.a: In those days the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed or conquered by another people.

questions.q: What did Daniel say about the dream and its interpretation?
questions.a: Daniel said the dream was certain and its interpretation was confirmed.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar command to be done for Daniel after he finished telling the king the dream and its interpretation?
questions.a: The king commanded an offering to be made and incense be offered up to Daniel.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar say concerning Daniel’s God?
questions.a: Nebuchadnezzar said Daniel’s God is the God of gods, the Lord of kings and the one who reveals secrets.

questions.q: What did the king do for Daniel after the interpretation?
questions.a: The king made Daniel great, gave him many gifts, and made him ruler over the province of Babylon and chief over all the wise men of Babylon.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do after Daniel made a request of the king?
questions.a: The king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be administrators over the province of Babylon.

commentary.text: Nebuchadnezzar's dream. (Dan. 2:1-13) It is revealed to Daniel. (Dan. 2:14-23) He obtains admission to the king. (Dan. 2:24-30) The dream and the interpretation. (Dan. 2:31-45) Honours to Daniel and his friends. (Dan. 2:46-49)

Dan. 2:1-13 The greatest men are most open to cares and troubles of mind, which disturb their repose in the night, while the sleep of the labouring man is sweet and sound. We know not the uneasiness of many who live in great pomp, and, as others vainly think, in pleasure also. The king said that his learned men must tell him the dream itself, or they should all be put to death as deceivers. Men are more eager to ask as to future events, than to learn the way of salvation or the path of duty; yet foreknowledge of future events increases anxiety and trouble. Those who deceived, by pretending to do what they could not do, were sentenced to death, for not being able to do what they did not pretend to.

Dan. 2:14-23 Daniel humbly prayed that God would discover to him the king's dream, and the meaning of it. Praying friends are valuable friends; and it well becomes the greatest and best men to desire the prayers of others. Let us show that we value our friends, and their prayers. They were particular in prayer. And whatever we pray for, we can expect nothing but as the gift of God's mercies. God gives us leave in prayer to tell our wants and burdens. Their plea with God was, the peril they were in. The mercy Daniel and his fellows prayed for, was bestowed. The fervent prayers of righteous men avail much. Daniel was thankful to God for making known that to him, which saved the lives of himself and his fellows. How much more should we be thankful to God, for making known the great salvation of the soul to those who are not among the worldly wise and prudent!

Dan. 2:24-30 Daniel takes away the king's opinion of his magicians and soothsayers. The insufficiency of creatures should drive us to the all-sufficiency of the Creator. There is One who can do that for us, and make known that to us, which none on earth can, particularly the work of redemption, and the secret designs of God's love to us therein. Daniel confirmed the king in his opinion, that the dream was of great consequence, relating to the affairs and changes of this lower world. Let those whom God has highly favoured and honoured, lay aside all opinion of their own wisdom and worthiness, that the Lord alone may be praised for the good they have and do.

Dan. 2:31-45 This image represented the kingdoms of the earth, that should successively rule the nations, and influence the affairs of the Jewish church. 1. The head of gold signified the Chaldean empire, then in being. 2. The breast and arms of silver signified the empire of the Medes and Persians. 3. The belly and thighs of brass signified the Grecian empire, founded by Alexander. 4. The legs and feet of iron signified the Roman empire. The Roman empire branched into ten kingdoms, as the toes of these feet. Some were weak as clay, others strong as iron. Endeavours have often been used to unite them, for strengthening the empire, but in vain. The stone cut out without hands, represented the kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ, which should be set up in the kingdoms of the world, upon the ruins of Satan's kingdom in them. This was the Stone which the builders refused, because it was not cut out by their hands, but it is become the head stone of the corner. Of the increase of Christ's government and peace there shall be no end. The Lord shall reign, not only to the end of time, but when time and days shall be no more. As far as events have gone, the fulfilling this prophetic vision has been most exact and undeniable; future ages shall witness this Stone destroying the image, and filling the whole earth.

Dan. 2:46-49 It is our business to direct attention to the Lord, as the Author and Giver of every good gift. Many have thoughts of the Divine power and majesty, who do not think of serving God themselves. But all should strive, that God may be glorified, and the best interests of mankind furthered.
